summary: The SI unit for amount of substance: exactly 6.02214076 × 10²³ entities.
detail: Fixed in 2019 by the Avogadro constant, so a mole of any substance contains that many atoms, molecules or ions.

summary: 6.02214076 × 10²³ per mole — the number of particles in one mole of a substance.
The mass of one mole of a substance, in grams per mole; numerically equal to the relative molecular mass.
detail: Water H₂O: 2 × 1.008 + 15.999 = 18.015 g/mol. Multiply moles by molar mass to get grams.

summary: The amount of solute per unit volume of solution, usually moles per litre.
detail: Dilution follows c₁V₁ = c₂V₂: adding solvent changes the volume but not the number of moles.

summary: A measure of acidity: pH = −log₁₀[H⁺], with 7 neutral at 25 °C.
detail: Below 7 is acidic, above is basic. Because it is logarithmic, each unit is a tenfold change in hydrogen-ion concentration — stomach acid at pH 1.5 is a million times more acidic than pure water.

summary: The number of protons in an atom's nucleus, which fixes which element it is.
detail: Carbon always has 6 protons; adding a neutron gives an isotope, adding a proton makes a different element.

summary: The total number of protons and neutrons in a nucleus.
detail: Carbon-14 has a mass number of 14: six protons and eight neutrons.

summary: Atoms of the same element with different numbers of neutrons, so the same chemistry but a different mass.
detail: Chemically near-identical, but some isotopes are radioactive (carbon-14, uranium-235) and others stable (carbon-12, carbon-13).

summary: The constant in the ideal gas law, 8.314462618… J/(mol·K).
1.380649 × 10⁻²³ J/K — the bridge between temperature and energy per particle.
detail: Exact since 2019, when the kelvin was defined through it. Average thermal energy per particle is roughly (3/2)k_BT.

summary: Using the ratios in a balanced chemical equation to work out how much of each substance reacts.
detail: 2H₂ + O₂ → 2H₂O means two moles of hydrogen react with one mole of oxygen to give two moles of water — masses convert through molar mass.

summary: The minimum energy colliding particles need before a reaction can happen.
detail: Catalysts lower it without being consumed. Raising temperature by 10 °C typically doubles the rate, because more particles clear the barrier.

summary: Moles of solute per kilogram of solvent — concentration that does not change with temperature.
detail: Molality is used for boiling-point elevation and freezing-point depression because it is defined by mass, not volume.

summary: How strongly an atom pulls shared electrons towards itself, measured on the Pauling scale.
detail: Fluorine is the highest at 3.98. Big differences make ionic bonds; similar values make covalent ones.
